name: Anti-Dilution and Down-Round Adjustment

positioning.oneLineSummary: Parses the exact down-round trigger, formula, denominator, carve-outs, waiver, and conversion consequence before calculating redistribution.
positioning.productLabel: Anti-Dilution Lens — based on Feld and Mendelson's public term-sheet materials
notAClaimOf: anti-dilution protecting against all ownership dilution
weighted average having one universal formula
full ratchet or market frequency determining deal quality

attribution.display: Based on Brad Feld and Jason Mendelson's public anti-dilution materials

neutralParaphrase: When a financing may trigger anti-dilution, read the exact conversion-price adjustment mechanism. Distinguish full ratchet from weighted average, broad from narrow denominator, and included issuances from carve-outs or waivers; then calculate class-by-class ownership and exit-payoff effects together with financing alternatives.

locator.value: Full ratchet, weighted-average equation, broad/narrow CSO, carve-outs, waivers, and financing incentives
Q3 2024 sample prevalence of broad-based weighted-average protection and absence of full ratchet
Current model-document alternatives and starting-point disclaimer

requiredConditions: The protected class, original conversion price, and adjustment clause are available.
The new issuance price, amount, tranches, consideration, and exempt issuances are defined.
Broad/narrow denominator and all convertible securities are reconciled.
Waiver, class vote, pay-to-play, recapitalization, and financing alternatives are modeled.

requiredEvidence.description: Exact formula, protected class, conversion price, denominator, carve-outs, waiver threshold, and tranche rule.
New price, amount, securities, closings, noncash consideration, pool changes, and participating holders.
Down-round, waiver, pay-to-play, recapitalization, bridge, and no-financing scenarios.

decisionQuestions: Is the formula full ratchet or which weighted-average variant?
What counts in the denominator and which issuances are carved out?
Can the class waive protection, and who votes?
How does the adjustment change ownership and exit payoff for every class?
How do waiver, pay-to-play, recap, bridge, and failure-to-finance compare?
positiveSignals: The exact formula and denominator are extracted.
All carve-outs, waivers, tranches, and convertibles are modeled.
Ownership and waterfall effects are shown by class.
The financing is compared with realistic alternatives.
Counsel confirms the trigger and calculation.
redFlags: The system assumes broad-based weighted average from a label.
Full ratchet is modeled without amount and price states.
Carve-outs or class waiver are omitted.
Anti-dilution is described as protection from all dilution.
The company rejects essential financing solely to preserve headline valuation.
disconfirmingEvidence: The issuance is exempt or waived.
A tranche definition changes effective trigger timing.
Pay-to-play changes rights before anti-dilution applies.
The cap table denominator differs from the model.
No-financing or debt alternative produces worse stakeholder outcomes.
contraindications: Do not calculate from the words anti-dilution alone.
Do not infer carve-outs or waiver.
Do not treat market frequency as the deal's rule.
Do not let the LLM calculate the adjustment.

instructions: Parse the protected security and exact adjustment clause.
Reconcile the pre-financing denominator and new issuance.
Run trigger, carve-out, waiver, and pay-to-play gates.
Calculate conversion-price, ownership, and waterfall changes by scenario.
Report financing alternatives and counsel questions to Fund Policy.

sourceReliability.low: Only a term label or market benchmark is available.
sourceReliability.medium: Clause and financing terms exist but denominator or waiver is incomplete.
sourceReliability.high: Executed clause, cap table, new terms, waivers, and counsel review reconcile.

evidenceStrength.medium: A bounded adjustment is possible with one explicit interpretation.
evidenceStrength.high: All conversion and payoff effects are deterministic.

evidenceCoverage.low: Only old and new prices are known.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Formula and amount are covered but exemptions, waiver, or alternatives are partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: Formula, denominator, issuance, tranches, carve-outs, waiver, pay-to-play, and alternatives are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.medium: Protection exists with custom or ambiguous drafting.
applicabilityConfidence.high: The trigger and formula are explicit.

judgmentConfidence.low: Only a potential trigger warning is defensible.
judgmentConfidence.medium: A bounded ownership effect can be shown.
judgmentConfidence.high: The adjustment and stakeholder trade-offs are reproducible.

promotionRequirements: Golden-case tests for all supported formula modes.
Validate ordering with pay-to-play and recapitalization.
empiricalQualifications: Term prevalence shifts with market cycles.
The financing alternative and runway can matter more than the adjustment alone.

rights.notes: Public author doctrine is neutrally paraphrased; the exact formula comes only from executed documents.
